topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and states its learning objectives.

topics.label: Biological origins of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arising in susceptible cells can drive clonal evolution within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental influences on cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine evidence for environmental contributions to cancer risk and the difficulty of distinguishing those contributions from chance and genetic susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious agents and cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmental DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental exposures damage DNA and generate mutations through direct action or cellular processing.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-inducing initiation from the promotion of tumour growth through a supportive cellular environment.

topics.label: Context-dependent carcinogen susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological context shapes susceptibility to carcinogens, concluding with a recap that reinforces tissue and developmental specificity.

topics.label: Methods for investigating carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how carcinogenic effects can be identified and evaluated while accounting for the limitations of the available evidence.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and framing exposure decisions as a balance of risks and benefits.
